lessons.name: Agile Justin
lessons.summary: Agile Justin is DLR's wheeled two-armed humanoid that learns dextrous manipulation with AI, touch sensing and torque-controlled joints.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Agile Justin is DLR's wheeled two-armed humanoid that learns dextrous manipulation with AI, touch sensing and torque-controlled joints.

![Agile Justin assembling an object in the DLR lab](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-agile-justin.webp)
*Agile Justin assembling an object in the DLR lab. Source: [DLR Agile Justin page](https://www.dlr.de/en/rm/research/robotic-systems/humanoids/agile-justin), CC BY-NC-ND 3.0.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A research flagship shows the full stack:** perception, planning, whole-body control and learning run on one mobile robot.
- **Touch is a first-class sensor:** a **tactile skin** covers the body and hands, so learning can use contact, not only cameras.
- **It is the successor to Rollin' Justin:** DLR added tactile skin, a wireless compute cluster and the aRDx real-time framework.

> **Key idea:** Agile Justin pairs strong hardware feedback (joint torque and touch) with learned skills, so policies can react to contact.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Mobile platform with 8 degrees of freedom:** wheels move the robot and adjust its stance.
- **Two 7-DOF arms and two 12-DOF hands:** the upper body adds a 3-DOF torso and 2-DOF neck.
- **Torque sensors sit in all joints:** the controller feels forces and runs whole-body control at 1 kHz.
- **Head cameras give 3D vision:** two stereo cameras plus an RGB-D camera.
- **Learning runs in DLR's Autonomous Learning Lab:** generative AI and deep reinforcement learning train skills, using onboard Xeon CPUs plus external GPU servers.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Height** | 1.91 m |
| **Weight** | 45 kg upper body + 150 kg platform |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 53 |
| **Nominal load** | 15 kg |
| **Speed** | 2 m/s |
| **Battery runtime** | > 60 min |
| **Workspace** | Floor to 2.7 m |

## Key terms

- **Degree of freedom (DOF)**: one independent joint motion the robot can control.
- **Torque sensor**: a sensor measuring the twisting force at a joint.
- **Tactile skin**: a sensor layer that detects touch on the robot's surface.
- **Whole-body control**: one controller coordinating base, torso, arms and head together.
- **Deep reinforcement learning**: learning behaviours by trial and reward with neural networks.

## Getting started

1. **Read DLR's Agile Justin page** and note which sensors feed each skill.
2. **Watch the touch-classification video** and identify the input data and the predicted label.
3. **Compare with Rollin' Justin** to see what the upgrades changed.
4. **Think of it as a microservice cluster:** sensors, controllers and learners exchange real-time messages, like services on a fast message bus.

## Used in

- **DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics research:** dextrous manipulation, in-hand learning and household or astronaut assistance scenarios.
- **Published tactile in-hand learning:** DLR lists an ICRA 2023 paper on reinforcement learning with tactile feedback.

lessons.name: AI Worker
lessons.summary: AI Worker is ROBOTIS's open-source semi-humanoid on a swerve-drive base, trained by imitation and reinforcement learning for factory tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

AI Worker is ROBOTIS's open-source semi-humanoid on a swerve-drive base, trained by imitation and reinforcement learning for factory tasks.

![ROBOTIS AI Worker hardware overview](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-ai-worker.webp)
*ROBOTIS AI Worker hardware overview. Source: [ROBOTIS AI Worker hardware docs](https://ai.robotis.com/ai_worker/hardware_ai_worker.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Everything is open:** ROBOTIS publishes source code, simulation and data tools, with ROS 2 packages under Apache-2.0 on GitHub.
- **It speaks LeRobot formats:** the training workflow stores datasets in a **LeRobot** dataset folder.
- **It targets real work:** ROBOTIS cites wiring-harness assembly, welding and inspection.

> **Key idea:** AI Worker is a full pipeline, not only a robot: teleoperation, dataset recording, training and deployment come documented together.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **DYNAMIXEL actuators move every joint:** ROBOTIS uses its own Y, P and X series servos.
- **Two 7-DOF arms with grippers:** each carries 3 kg nominally, 5 kg peak.
- **A swerve-drive base:** each wheel steers independently, so the robot can move in any direction.
- **Sensors include 3 RGB-D cameras:** a ZED Mini in the head, two RealSense D405 on the wrists, plus two LiDARs and an IMU.
- **A Jetson AGX Orin 32GB runs ROS 2:** a leader device lets a human teleoperate it.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Mobile model** | FFW-SG2 |
| **Size** | 604 × 602 × 1623 mm |
| **Weight** | 90 kg |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 25 |
| **Arm payload** | 3 kg nominal per arm |
| **Max speed** | 1.5 m/s |
| **Battery** | 25 V, 80 Ah (2,040 Wh) |
| **Computer** | NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32GB |

## Key terms

- **Semi-humanoid**: a robot with a human-like upper body on a non-walking base.
- **Swerve drive**: a base where every wheel both drives and steers.
- **RGB-D camera**: a camera giving colour plus per-pixel depth.
- **Sim2Real**: training in simulation, then running on the real robot.
- **ROS 2**: Robot Operating System 2, a middleware for robot software.

## Getting started

1. **Read the introduction and hardware pages** in the ROBOTIS docs.
2. **Clone the GitHub repository** and browse the ROS 2 packages.
3. **Follow the model-training guide:** it uses the Physical AI Tools Docker image and a web UI.
4. **Think of the Docker image like a CI runner:** a reproducible environment that turns datasets into trained models.

## Used in

- **ROBOTIS demos:** Sim2Real with NVIDIA Isaac Sim and GR00T, shown in its AI WORKER video series.
- **Industrial pilots:** ROBOTIS targets harness assembly, welding and inspection tasks.

lessons.name: AISPRID leaf-removal robot
lessons.summary: The AISPRID robot autonomously removes leaves from tomato plants in greenhouses, working day and night and changing rows by itself.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The AISPRID robot autonomously removes leaves from tomato plants in greenhouses, working day and night and changing rows by itself.

![AISPRID robot working between greenhouse tomato rows](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-aisprid.webp)
*AISPRID robot working between greenhouse tomato rows. Source: [AISPRID website](https://aisprid.com/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A real deployed robot:** AISPRID says more than 50 robots work daily at major growers in France, Belgium and the Netherlands.
- **One narrow job done well:** **deleafing** takes about 40% of a harvest team's time, according to a grower quoted by AISPRID.
- **It shows a European agri-robotics path:** vision, a precise tool and autonomy in a structured greenhouse.

> **Key idea:** A specialised mobile manipulator succeeds by mastering one repetitive, well-defined task in a structured environment.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A mobile base drives along greenhouse rows:** the robot switches rows autonomously.
- **Vision finds the leaves to remove:** the company describes its robot as smart and AI-driven.
- **A cutting tool cuts close to the stem:** the cut is precise and near the plant.
- **A remote app monitors the fleet:** growers watch progress from a phone or computer.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Task** | Leaf removal on greenhouse tomatoes |
| **Working height** | Up to 2 m |
| **Share of deleafing delegated** | Up to 80% |
| **Robots in daily use** | More than 50 |
| **Countries** | France, Belgium, Netherlands |
| **Price** | unknown |

> **Watch out:** Growth numbers like 50 robots and 80% delegation come from AISPRID itself, not an independent study.

## Key terms

- **Deleafing**: removing lower leaves from tomato plants so fruit and air flow improve.
- **Autonomous navigation**: moving through an environment without a human driver.
- **End effector**: the tool at the end of a robot arm, here a cutter.
- **Fleet monitoring**: tracking several robots' status remotely.

## Getting started

1. **Watch AISPRID's main video** to see the robot cut leaves in a row.
2. **List the robot's sense, decide and act steps** for one leaf.
3. **Picture it as a cron job with eyes:** it repeats the same loop all night, but each cut depends on vision.
4. **Read the AISPRID site** for deployment numbers and the planned battery-swap station.

## Used in

- **Tomato growers' cooperatives:** France, Belgium and the Netherlands, per AISPRID.
- **GreenTech Amsterdam 2026:** AISPRID exhibited the robot there, as shown in its video.

lessons.name: AgileX Cobot Magic (Mobile ALOHA kit)
lessons.summary: AgileX Cobot Magic is a commercial whole-body teleoperation kit based on Mobile ALOHA, built for two-arm data collection and embodied AI.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

AgileX Cobot Magic is a commercial whole-body teleoperation kit based on Mobile ALOHA, built for two-arm data collection and embodied AI.

![AgileX Cobot Magic bimanual teleoperation platform](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-cobot-magic.webp)
*AgileX Cobot Magic bimanual teleoperation platform. Source: [AgileX COBOT MAGIC product page](https://global.agilex.ai/products/cobot-magic-bimanual-teleoperation-platform-mobile-aloha), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A ready-made data factory:** it packages the Stanford **Mobile ALOHA** recipe as a product instead of a parts list.
- **Two-arm demonstrations feed imitation learning:** a person drives leader arms, and the robot records what the follower arms see and do.
- **It shares its base with the original:** Mobile ALOHA was built on an AgileX TRACER mobile base.

> **Key idea:** Cobot Magic is a recording rig first: the human demonstrations it captures are the raw material for learned policies.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Four PiPER arms with 6 DoF each:** two leader arms are moved by the operator, two follower arms copy them.
- **A TRACER 2.0 mobile base drives the platform:** the operator can move while manipulating.
- **Wrist and top cameras record the scene:** these images become the training inputs.
- **An onboard PC runs the Mobile ALOHA software stack:** it logs joint states and camera streams together.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Based on** | Mobile ALOHA (open source) |
| **Arms** | 4 × PiPER, 6 DoF each |
| **Mobile base** | AgileX TRACER 2.0 |
| **Cameras** | Wrist and top views |
| **Main use** | Bimanual teleoperation and data collection |
| **Price** | unknown |

## Key terms

- **Bimanual**: using two arms together on one task.
- **Leader-follower teleoperation**: a human moves leader arms and follower arms mirror them.
- **Embodied AI**: AI that perceives and acts through a physical body.
- **Episode**: one recorded demonstration from start to finish.
- **Imitation learning**: training a policy to copy recorded human demonstrations.

## Getting started

1. **Read the AgileX product page** and list which parts are leaders and followers.
2. **Study the Mobile ALOHA project page** to understand the original training recipe.
3. **Think of each episode like a log file:** synchronized camera frames and joint values, replayed later for training.
4. **Watch the unboxing video** before planning any lab purchase.

## Used in

- **AgileX Robotics demonstrations:** 24-hour clothes-folding tests and screw fastening shown on its channel.
- **Embodied AI research labs:** the vendor positions it for robot data collection and bimanual manipulation.

lessons.name: DXTR
lessons.summary: DXTR is Duatic's dual-arm mobile manipulator for intralogistics, lifting up to 30 kg with two coordinated arms on an autonomous base.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

DXTR is Duatic's dual-arm mobile manipulator for intralogistics, lifting up to 30 kg with two coordinated arms on an autonomous base.

![Duatic DXTR dual-arm mobile manipulator](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-dxtr.webp)
*Duatic DXTR dual-arm mobile manipulator. Source: [Duatic website](https://www.duatic.com/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Built for existing warehouses:** Duatic says it needs no racking changes, safety cages or fixed pick station.
- **Two arms share heavy loads:** together they lift up to 30 kg, more than many single cobot arms.
- **It comes from a European startup:** Duatic is based in Glattbrugg, Switzerland.

> **Key idea:** DXTR is modular: an arm, a torso and a base are separate products combined into one robot.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **DynaArm provides the arms:** an ultra-light quasi-direct-drive arm that is **backdrivable** and uses impedance control.
- **DuaTorso holds both arms and vision:** it forms the dual-arm upper body.
- **DuaRover is the autonomous base:** it carries up to 200 kg on top.
- **Impedance control makes contact gentle:** the arm behaves like a spring instead of a rigid machine.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Maker** | Duatic (Switzerland) |
| **Arms** | 2 × DynaArm |
| **Dual-arm lift** | Up to 30 kg |
| **Base payload on top** | Up to 200 kg |
| **Target use** | Intralogistics |
| **Price** | unknown |

## Key terms

- **Intralogistics**: moving goods inside a warehouse or factory.
- **Quasi-direct drive**: a motor with little or no gearbox, so joints stay responsive.
- **Backdrivable**: a joint you can push by hand, letting the robot feel external forces.
- **Impedance control**: controlling how stiff or soft a robot reacts to contact.

## Getting started

1. **Watch the DXTR warehouse video** and note how both arms share a box.
2. **Read Duatic's site** to see the three modules.
3. **Think of the modules like libraries:** arm, torso and base are composed through clear interfaces.
4. **Watch the DynaArm video** to understand backdrivable joints.

## Used in

- **Warehouse operations:** Duatic shows DXTR handling goods in a warehouse demonstration.
- **Duatic Alpha:** a related system grasps 20 kg bags, according to Duatic.

lessons.name: Eno
lessons.summary: Eno is Genesis AI's general-purpose robot: a wheeled base, a foldable tower and two human-sized hands driven by the GENE foundation model.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Eno is Genesis AI's general-purpose robot: a wheeled base, a foldable tower and two human-sized hands driven by the GENE foundation model.

![Genesis AI's Eno robot in the lab](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-eno.webp)
*Genesis AI's Eno robot in the lab. Source: [Genesis AI website](https://www.genesis.ai/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A European bet on non-humanoid design:** Genesis AI, a French startup founded in early 2025, chose wheels instead of legs.
- **Hands get the complexity:** each hand matches human size with 20 active, **back-drivable** degrees of freedom.
- **Model-first company:** Eno runs **GENE**, the company's own foundation model, trained with its simulation platform.

> **Key idea:** Eno puts its mechanical budget into hands and its intelligence into one foundation model, instead of walking legs.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A wheeled base moves the robot:** wheels are simpler and stabler than legs.
- **A foldable tower lifts the arms:** Eno folds to the size of a checked bag.
- **Two dexterous hands do the work:** 20 active back-drivable DOF each.
- **GENE controls behaviour:** Genesis World 1.0 provides simulation for training.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Maker** | Genesis AI (France) |
| **Base** | Wheeled |
| **Hand DOF** | 20 active, back-drivable |
| **Folded size** | Checked-bag size |
| **Model** | GENE foundation model |
| **Access** | Waitlist |
| **Price** | unknown |

> **Watch out:** Eno is a 2026 product; availability, price and real-world performance are still unknown.

## Key terms

- **Foundation model**: a large model trained on broad data and adapted to many tasks.
- **Back-drivable**: a joint that can be pushed by outside forces, making contact safer.
- **Dexterous hand**: a multi-finger hand able to manipulate objects.
- **Simulation platform**: software that models physics to train robots virtually.

## Getting started

1. **Watch Meet Eno** to see the form factor.
2. **Read the Reuters report** for funding and deployment plans.
3. **Think of GENE like a pretrained LLM:** one general model adapted to tasks instead of hand-coded scripts.
4. **Join the waitlist** only after checking availability; deployment is planned for late 2026.

## Used in

- **First targets are logistics and manufacturing:** Reuters reports later plans for hotels, hospitals and consumers.
- **Genesis AI's own lab:** dozens of units have been built, according to Reuters.

lessons.name: Mobile ALOHA
lessons.summary: Mobile ALOHA is Stanford's low-cost whole-body teleoperation system that puts two-arm ALOHA on a mobile base to learn household tasks from demonstrations.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Mobile ALOHA is Stanford's low-cost whole-body teleoperation system that puts two-arm ALOHA on a mobile base to learn household tasks from demonstrations.

![Mobile ALOHA performing household tasks](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-mobile-aloha.webp)
*Mobile ALOHA performing household tasks. Source: [Mobile ALOHA project page](https://mobile-aloha.github.io/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A landmark in learned mobile manipulation:** Zipeng Fu, Tony Z. Zhao and Chelsea Finn published it at CoRL 2024.
- **It made data collection cheap:** an operator drives the base while steering both arms.
- **It inspired products:** AgileX Cobot Magic (Mobile ALOHA kit) packages the same idea.

> **Key idea:** Fifty demonstrations per task, plus co-training with static ALOHA data, can raise success rates by up to 90%.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Bimanual manipulation with leader-follower arms:** an operator moves leader arms, and followers copy them.
- **An AgileX TRACER base adds mobility:** the operator is tethered and pushes the base.
- **Cameras record every episode:** the open launch files start four robots and four cameras.
- **Supervised behaviour cloning trains the policy:** the repo includes a fork of ACT for Mobile ALOHA.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Authors** | Zipeng Fu, Tony Z. Zhao, Chelsea Finn |
| **Venue** | CoRL 2024 |
| **Demonstrations per task** | 50 |
| **Success gain from co-training** | Up to 90% |
| **Software** | ROS 1 Noetic on Ubuntu 20.04 |
| **Code** | Open source on GitHub |

> **Watch out:** The arms have no brakes: the repo warns joints collapse when torque turns off.

## Key terms

- **Behaviour cloning**: supervised learning that maps observations to recorded human actions.
- **Co-training**: training on the new dataset together with an existing related dataset.
- **ACT**: Action Chunking with Transformers, a policy predicting short action sequences.
- **Whole-body teleoperation**: controlling the base and both arms at once.

## Getting started

1. **Watch the main video** to see the tasks.
2. **Read the arXiv paper**, focusing on the co-training result.
3. **Treat co-training like transfer learning:** extra data from a related domain improves a small dataset.
4. **Clone the GitHub repo** and read the hardware setup notes.

## Used in

- **Learned household tasks:** sauteing shrimp, storing pots in a cabinet, calling an elevator and rinsing a pan.
- **Learn a mobile cabinet interaction:** a project that builds on this kind of task.
- **Commercial follow-up:** AgileX Cobot Magic (Mobile ALOHA kit).

lessons.name: Rollin' Justin
lessons.summary: Rollin' Justin is DLR's wheeled humanoid with two torque-controlled arms and hands, built for household-service and astronaut-assistance research.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Rollin' Justin is DLR's wheeled humanoid with two torque-controlled arms and hands, built for household-service and astronaut-assistance research.

![Rollin' Justin, DLR's mobile humanoid](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-rollin-justin.webp)
*Rollin' Justin, DLR's mobile humanoid. Source: [DLR Rollin' Justin page](https://www.dlr.de/en/rm/research/robotic-systems/humanoids/rollin-justin), CC BY 3.0.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A long-running reference platform:** first shown publicly in 2008, it shaped how researchers build **compliant** mobile manipulators.
- **It mixes service tasks and space research:** DLR tested it in household chores and in teleoperation from the ISS.
- **It shows why wheels help:** a wheeled base gives stability for heavy, precise two-arm work.

> **Key idea:** Rollin' Justin is compliant: torque-controlled joints let it yield to contact instead of fighting it.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Wheeled base with 8 degrees of freedom:** four spring-borne wheels, according to Wikipedia, carry the robot.
- **Arms come from the DLR LWR III:** two 7-DOF lightweight arms carry DLR Hand II hands with 12 DOF each.
- **Torque sensors are in nearly all joints:** two IMUs track motion and orientation.
- **Cameras map the scene:** two stereo and five RGB-D cameras give 3D perception.
- **A hierarchical whole-body controller ranks tasks:** lower-priority goals run in the null space of higher ones.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Height** | 1.91 m |
| **Weight** | approx. 200 kg |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 51 |
| **Nominal load** | 20 kg |
| **Speed** | 2 m/s |
| **Battery runtime** | > 60 min |
| **Workspace** | Floor to 2.7 m |

## Key terms

- **Compliance**: the ability of a robot to yield softly when it meets a force.
- **Null space**: joint motions that do not disturb a higher-priority task.
- **IMU**: inertial measurement unit, a sensor measuring acceleration and rotation.
- **Teleoperation**: a person controlling a robot remotely.
- **Supervised autonomy**: the robot executes tasks alone while a human gives high-level commands.

## Getting started

1. **Read the DLR Rollin' Justin page** and match each sensor to a task.
2. **Watch the cleaning-task video** and list the steps the planner chains together.
3. **Treat task priorities like process scheduling:** an urgent task preempts others, as a kernel scheduler does.
4. **Compare with Agile Justin** to see how the design evolved.

## Used in

- **DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics research:** whole-body control and household service tasks such as cleaning.
- **METERON SUPVIS Justin:** astronauts on the ISS commanded it as a robotic co-worker on Earth.
- **Catching experiments:** Wikipedia reports catching thrown balls with about 80% success.

lessons.name: Galaxea R1
lessons.summary: Galaxea R1 is a wheeled, two-arm research robot for collecting demonstrations and learning coordinated household manipulation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Galaxea R1 is a wheeled, two-arm research robot for collecting demonstrations and learning coordinated household manipulation.

![Galaxea R1 series wheeled dual-arm robots](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-galaxea-r1.webp)
*R1 series robots with articulated torsos and wheeled bases. Source: [Galaxea Dynamics](https://galaxea-dynamics.com/products/galaxea-r1-series-pioneering-wheeled-dual-arm-robotics), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Learning needs a body:** Stanford's BEHAVIOR Robot Suite (BRS) uses R1 to study household work, including shelving boxes and handling clothing.
- **Whole-body coordination matters:** Moving the base changes where the hands can reach; an arm-only policy cannot describe the complete task.
- **Software is accessible:** BRS publishes control code and demonstration-collection tools, giving us something concrete to inspect without buying hardware.

> **Key idea:** A useful household action coordinates the base, torso and hands rather than treating each as an independent robot.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Two arms and grippers:** The grippers open and close around objects; the torso changes the arms' working position.
- **An omnidirectional base:** Wheels let the robot move across the floor in different directions.
- **JoyLo collects demonstrations:** A person steers the robot using small matching arm linkages and Joy-Con controllers.
- **Think of an API request:** BRS groups arm, gripper, torso and base commands into one control call, like related fields in a structured request.
- **Keep variants separate:** These manufacturer specifications describe R1 Pro; the listed Lite version has six degrees of freedom per arm instead.

| Specification | R1 Pro manufacturer listing |
| --- | --- |
| **Mass including battery** | 126 kg |
| **Arm degrees of freedom** | 7 per arm |
| **Arm radius with gripper** | 860 mm |
| **Rated single-arm payload** | 3.5 kg |
| **Maximum chassis speed** | 1.5 m/s |

## Key terms

- **Degree of freedom**: one independently controlled movement, such as rotating a joint.
- **Teleoperation**: a person controlling the robot remotely.
- **Policy**: software mapping observations to robot actions.
- **Payload**: the load a robot is specified to carry.

## Getting started

1. **Watch the BRS rollouts** and identify when the base, torso and arms move together.
2. **Work a command example:** Two seven-joint arms require fourteen arm targets, before adding torso, base and gripper commands.
3. **Read the free BRS control repository:** Find the separate command fields before trying any physical movement.
4. **Budget realistically:** The series page advertises from $39,999 but directs business and education purchases to sales, not direct checkout.

## Used in

- **BEHAVIOR Robot Suite:** R1 supports whole-body teleoperation and learned household activities.
- **Galaxea AI (Galaxea Dynamics):** The builder supplies the hardware; BRS provides a separate open research stack.

lessons.name: Galbot G1
lessons.summary: Galbot G1 is a wheeled, two-arm robot designed to pick, move and deliver objects in retail, industrial and household settings.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Galbot G1 is a wheeled, two-arm robot designed to pick, move and deliver objects in retail, industrial and household settings.

![Galbot G1 robot with two arms and wheeled base](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-galbot-g1.webp)
*G1 hardware from the manufacturer. Source: [Galbot](http://www.galbot.com/g1/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A concrete retail robot:** CGTN reported G1 picking and packaging medicines in a Beijing pharmacy in March 2026.
- **Data is available to study:** RoboCOIN publishes a G1 demonstration dataset for putting steamed buns into a steamer and replacing its lid.
- **Separate robot from model:** Galbot is the builder; G1 is hardware, while its product page names AstraBrain as its intelligence system.

> **Key idea:** A retail robot must connect perception and grasping to a complete delivery workflow, not just lift an object once.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A lifting body and two arms:** Height adjustment and articulated arms extend the workspace beyond a fixed tabletop.
- **Cameras near the action:** The manufacturer lists a head stereo camera and wrist depth cameras, which measure distance as well as appearance.
- **A mobile base:** Four omnidirectional wheels move the body; laser ranging helps it perceive surrounding geometry.
- **Interchangeable tools:** Hands, suction tools or grippers can be fitted for different objects.
- **Like processing an order:** Identifying, picking, packaging and delivering a product are separate stages, like services in a backend workflow.

| Specification | Manufacturer listing |
| --- | --- |
| **Maximum height** | 1730 mm |
| **Body mass** | 92.5 kg |
| **Arm degrees of freedom** | 7 per arm |
| **Payload at wrist centre** | 5 kg per arm; 10 kg combined |
| **Maximum base speed** | 1.5 m/s |
| **Battery** | 48 V, 30 Ah |

## Key terms

- **Stereo camera**: two viewpoints used together to estimate depth.
- **End effector**: the tool attached to the arm, such as a gripper.
- **Episode**: one recorded attempt at a task.
- **State**: recorded measurements describing the robot at a moment.

## Getting started

1. **Open the free RoboCOIN dataset** and watch its task preview before reading the arrays.
2. **Inspect the action fields:** Fourteen arm-joint values plus two gripper values make sixteen action dimensions in this dataset.
3. **Compare state and action:** Its twenty-one state dimensions include torso and head measurements absent from that action vector.
4. **Check access with the maker:** Hardware price is unknown here; public data access does not imply owning or freely controlling a G1.

## Used in

- **Galbot retail workflows:** The pharmacy report describes product retrieval, packaging and placement into a pickup cabinet.
- **RoboCOIN:** G1 demonstrations provide a free starting point for understanding paired robot observations and actions.

lessons.name: HMND 01
lessons.summary: HMND 01 is Humanoid's industrial robot platform; its wheeled Alpha version has been tested moving containers in a Siemens factory.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

HMND 01 is Humanoid's industrial robot platform; its wheeled Alpha version has been tested moving containers in a Siemens factory.

![HMND 01 Alpha working at the Siemens factory](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-hmnd-01.webp)
*The wheeled Alpha platform in the Siemens pilot. Source: [Humanoid](https://thehumanoid.ai/siemens-and-humanoid-bring-physical-ai-to-the-factory-floor-deploying-humanoids-in-industrial-operations-with-nvidia/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Measure useful work:** The April 2026 Siemens announcement reports container-handling throughput and success, rather than only showing a robot posing.
- **Integration is software work:** The robot must exchange information with factory systems and fit an existing production workflow.
- **Names overlap:** The Siemens source calls the robot HMND 01, HMND 01 Alpha and wheeled Alpha; these are not evidence of three separate machines.

> **Key idea:** Factory usefulness is a property of the whole workflow, including task assignment, robot motion and reliable handover.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Human-like upper body, wheeled base:** Arms manipulate containers while the mobile base transports them through the facility.
- **KinetIQ coordinates behaviour:** This is Humanoid's proprietary AI framework, not an open student programming library.
- **NVIDIA tools support development:** The announcement names Jetson Thor onboard computing, Isaac Sim simulation and Isaac Lab policy training.
- **Factory software connects the pieces:** Siemens Xcelerator supplies integration tools, including industrial communications and robot-control interfaces.
- **Think of a worker service:** A factory task arrives, the robot performs physical work, and the larger system coordinates what happens next.

| Siemens pilot metric | Reported result, April 2026 |
| --- | --- |
| **Site** | Electronics factory, Erlangen, Germany |
| **Task** | Picking, transporting and placing totes |
| **Throughput** | 60 tote moves per hour |
| **Uptime** | More than 8 hours |
| **Autonomous pick-and-place success** | Above 90% |

- **Worked interpretation:** Sixty moves per hour averages one move per minute; it does not say each grasp takes exactly sixty seconds.

## Key terms

- **Tote**: a container used to hold and transport parts.
- **Throughput**: completed work per unit of time.
- **Uptime**: time a system remains available for operation.
- **Simulation**: a software environment used to test or train behaviour before physical deployment.

## Getting started

1. **Watch the Siemens pilot video** and list the pick, transport and placement stages.
2. **Read the reported metrics:** Keep uptime separate from battery runtime and success rate.
3. **Sketch a free workflow model:** Represent waiting, fetching, moving and handing over as software states.
4. **Treat access as commercial:** A student purchase price and freely downloadable HMND 01 controller are unknown.

## Used in

- **Siemens:** The Erlangen test demonstrated autonomous logistics inside an operating electronics factory.
- **HMND 01 Alpha:** Read the related hardware lesson for the specific wheeled version rather than treating the platform name as another product.

lessons.name: HMND 01 Alpha
lessons.summary: HMND 01 Alpha is Humanoid's wheeled industrial robot for handling containers and connecting physical logistics to factory software.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

HMND 01 Alpha is Humanoid's wheeled industrial robot for handling containers and connecting physical logistics to factory software.

![HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled with arms on an omnidirectional base](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-hmnd-01-alpha.webp)
*Alpha Wheeled on its manufacturer's product page. Source: [Humanoid](https://thehumanoid.ai/hmnd-01-alpha-wheeled/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A specific platform, not a generic humanoid:** This lesson concerns Alpha Wheeled, not Humanoid's separately advertised bipedal robot.
- **Enterprise integration is tangible:** A 2026 SAP and Martur Fompak proof of concept connected warehouse task assignment directly to the robot.
- **Contracts are not deliveries:** The May 2026 Schaeffler agreement schedules staged deployment; its four-digit target by 2032 is not an already operating fleet.

> **Key idea:** A humanoid becomes useful industrial infrastructure when existing software can assign it meaningful work and evaluate the result.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Wheels provide mobility:** The omnidirectional base can move in different floor directions without walking.
- **Tools are modular:** The product page offers a twelve-degree-of-freedom five-finger hand or a one-degree-of-freedom parallel gripper.
- **Sensing surrounds manipulation:** Head depth sensors estimate distances; wrist cameras provide views near the handled object.
- **KinetIQ is the software stack:** Humanoid describes it as a proprietary framework for coordinating robots and their tasks.
- **Like an API integration:** In the SAP test, warehouse software sent tasks through the Joule agent layer to Humanoid's robot API.

| Specification | Alpha Wheeled product listing |
| --- | --- |
| **Mass** | 300 kg |
| **Height** | 220 cm |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 29 |
| **Maximum speed** | 2 m/s |
| **Average runtime** | 4 hours |
| **Payload** | 15 kg |

- **Configuration matters:** The SAP pilot used an 8 kg dual-arm payload limit, not the fifteen-kilogram figure on the product page.

## Key terms

- **Omnidirectional**: able to move in different directions across the floor.
- **Parallel gripper**: a tool whose opposing jaws move together to grip an object.
- **Proof of concept**: a bounded test showing whether an approach can work.
- **Robot-as-a-Service**: obtaining robot operation and supporting services through a service arrangement.

## Getting started

1. **Watch the SAP pilot:** Follow a task from warehouse instruction to physical delivery.
2. **Trace the example:** The robot receives a task, navigates to a pallet, retrieves a KLT parts box and delivers it to a trolley.
3. **Read the contract timeline:** Initial Schaeffler deployment is scheduled for December 2026 through June 2027.
4. **Plan access realistically:** The agreement uses Robot-as-a-Service; a public student hardware price is unknown.

## Used in

- **Schaeffler:** A phased deployment and actuator-supply agreement links the customer to Humanoid.
- **HMND 01:** The broader platform lesson examines the Siemens logistics pilot and its operational metrics.

lessons.name: Iggy Rob
lessons.summary: Iggy Rob is igus's wheeled, two-arm robot platform, offered in industrial and service variants rather than as a walking humanoid.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Iggy Rob is igus's wheeled, two-arm robot platform, offered in industrial and service variants rather than as a walking humanoid.

![Published igus illustration of Iggy Rob robots in a factory](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-iggy-rob.webp)
*Published robot illustration from igus's 2025 announcement. Source: [igus](https://press.igus.com/2025/04/29/iggy-rob-humanoid/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Components become a system:** The robot combines mobile transport, two ReBeL arms, sensing and control rather than requiring a new walking mechanism.
- **Versions matter:** The 2025 industrial announcement and June 2026 Home announcement describe different configurations and price points.
- **Software students have an entry point:** The product listing describes free movement simulation using igus Robot Control without connecting a physical Iggy Rob.

> **Key idea:** Reusing established arms and a mobile base shifts attention from inventing mechanics to integrating useful tasks.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Two ReBeL arms manipulate objects:** End effectors, the tools attached to the wrists, vary by configuration.
- **A wheeled base transports the body:** The June 2026 announcement identifies ReBeLMove Pro as the shared Industrial and Home platform.
- **Lidar and cameras guide motion:** Lidar measures distance with laser light; 3D cameras add object and scene depth information.
- **ROS 2 connects software:** This robotics communication framework helps integrate the robot with other systems.
- **Think of reusable modules:** Arms, base and sensors resemble libraries with separate responsibilities; the complete application must make their interfaces work together.

| Specification | June 2026 platform announcement |
| --- | --- |
| **Configured height range** | 1.30–1.70 m |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 16 |
| **Default arm payload** | 2.5 kg per arm |
| **Autonomous runtime** | Up to 8 hours |
| **ReBeLMove Pro base capacity** | Up to 250 kg |
| **Home announced starting price** | €55,000 |

- **Do not confuse capacities:** Two arms rated at 2.5 kg each do not let one arm lift five kilograms; the base capacity is another specification.

## Key terms

- **AMR**: autonomous mobile robot, a mobile platform that navigates without continuous manual steering.
- **End effector**: the working tool at an arm's tip.
- **Fleet management**: coordinating tasks across multiple robots.
- **Configuration**: the particular hardware and software options fitted to a robot.

## Getting started

1. **Watch the 2025 introduction** to picture the original industrial robot and its wheels.
2. **Compare the announcements:** The 2025 €47,999 target is not a current quote for the 2026 Home variant.
3. **Inspect the free simulation option** described on the product page before requesting hardware.
4. **Request a variant-specific trial:** igus describes a test-before-purchase programme; confirm tooling, payload and integration requirements together.

## Used in

- **Industrial automation at igus:** The announcements target transport, machine loading, reception and catering; these targets are not a list of verified customer deployments.
- **Industrial and Home variants:** The shared wheeled platform supports different task and interaction configurations.

lessons.name: LG CLOiD
lessons.summary: LG CLOiD is LG Electronics' wheeled home robot demonstrator, combining two dexterous arms with AI and connected-appliance control.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LG CLOiD is LG Electronics' wheeled home robot demonstrator, combining two dexterous arms with AI and connected-appliance control.

![LG CLOiD handling laundry beside household appliances](/img/lessons/robots_mobile_manipulator-lg-cloid.webp)
*CLOiD in LG's published laundry demonstration setting. Source: [LG Electronics](https://www.lg.com/global/newsroom/news/home-appliance-solution/lg-electronics-presents-lg-cloid-home-robot-to-demonstrate-zero-labor-home-at-ces-2026/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Housework combines many systems:** Retrieving food, operating appliances and folding laundry require both physical manipulation and coordination with the home.
- **Human spaces shape hardware:** LG selected a wheeled base for stability, safety and cost, with a tilting torso to adjust working height.
- **A demonstration is not a dev kit:** The January 2026 announcement describes CES demonstrations, not an open controller or an affordable student product.

> **Key idea:** A home robot needs both hands for physical work and software interfaces for coordinating the appliances around it.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **A head acts as a hub:** It contains computing, cameras, sensors, a display and a speaker for perception and interaction.
- **Arms and fingers handle objects:** Seven degrees of freedom per arm allow shoulder, elbow and wrist movements; fingers move independently.
- **The torso tilts:** This changes the arms' working height so they can reach objects from knee level upward.
- **Vision and language guide actions:** LG describes models for interpreting images and instructions, then producing physical behaviour.
- **ThinQ connects appliances:** Think of a robot as an application calling appliance APIs while its arms perform steps that software alone cannot.

| Specification | LG's January 2026 announcement |
| --- | --- |
| **Arms** | 2 |
| **Degrees of freedom per arm** | 7 |
| **Independently actuated fingers per hand** | 5 |
| **Mobility** | Autonomous wheeled base |
| **Torso movement** | Tilting height adjustment |
| **Retail price / shipping date** | Unknown |

- **Count the arm motions:** Two seven-degree-of-freedom arms provide fourteen arm movements, before counting fingers, torso or base.

## Key terms

- **Degree of freedom**: one independently controlled movement.
- **VLM**: vision-language model, which turns visual input into language-based understanding.
- **VLA**: vision-language-action model, which connects visual and verbal inputs to physical actions.
- **Actuator**: a mechanism that turns a control signal and energy into movement.

## Getting started

1. **Watch LG's CES presentation** and distinguish appliance commands from physical grasping.
2. **Trace the breakfast example:** Retrieving milk and placing a croissant in an oven require different object interactions.
3. **Make a free task breakdown:** List observations, appliance commands and arm actions separately; no robot purchase is needed.
4. **Check access before planning:** A research SDK, retail price and shipping commitment are unknown in these sources.

## Used in

- **LG Electronics' Zero Labor Home vision:** CLOiD was presented for household scenarios at CES 2026.
- **ThinQ-connected homes:** The proposed system combines appliance orchestration with cooking and laundry demonstrations, rather than proving unrestricted household autonomy.
